content.value_statement: Roadmap planning can become disconnected from team capacity and sprint execution. This skill guides quarterly epics, milestones, sprint allocations, and capacity tradeoffs.
actual_capabilities: Uses a default capacity model of 20 points per developer per sprint.
Guides rough sizing for small, medium, and large milestones.
Describes collaborative planning commands for quarters, epics, and sprints.
Documents roadmap file locations under the .roadmap directory.
Maps epics and milestones to ClickUp tasks and subtasks for sync workflows.
limitations: It provides planning guidance, not detailed product specifications or QA tracking.
The default point model may need adjustment for each team.
ClickUp synchronization depends on related ClickUp sync commands outside this skill.
It does not independently verify delivery progress or repository state.

use_cases.title: Quarterly Product Planning
use_cases.description: Define strategic epics, rough sizes, and sprint timing before a quarter starts.

use_cases.title: Engineering Capacity Review
use_cases.description: Compare milestone estimates with developer availability and a planning buffer.

use_cases.title: Sprint Allocation Workshop
use_cases.description: Select milestones for an upcoming sprint while keeping the user in each decision.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a quarterly roadmap for my team. Ask for goals, team size, and major constraints before proposing epics.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate an Epic
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this epic into 2 to 4 milestones. Estimate each milestone in points and flag anything above 25 points.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Sprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the next two-week sprint using our available developers, current milestone estimates, and a 15 percent buffer.

prompt_templates.title: Sequence a Quarter
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this quarterly roadmap for sequencing risks, capacity conflicts, milestone dependencies, and ClickUp sync readiness.

output_examples.input: Plan a quarter for billing modernization with three developers.
output: The skill asks for goals, constraints, and team availability first.
It proposes epics, milestone sizes, sprint allocation, and a capacity buffer.
It flags any milestone that should be split before planning starts.

output_examples.input: Break the onboarding redesign epic into milestones.
output: The skill suggests 2 to 4 meaningful checkpoints.
It estimates each checkpoint using the small, medium, and large sizing guide.
It keeps the breakdown coarse enough to avoid replacing issue tracking.

output_examples.input: Check whether our sprint plan fits team capacity.
output: The skill compares planned points with available developer capacity.
It applies a recommended 15 percent buffer for unexpected work.
It identifies overcommitment and suggests moving lower-priority milestones.

best_practices: Confirm team capacity and planned absences before sizing a sprint.
Split milestones above 25 points before assigning them to a sprint.
Keep roadmap files focused on planning and use execution tools for detailed tasks.
anti_patterns: Do not use roadmap milestones as replacements for detailed issues or QA plans.
Do not fill every sprint to maximum capacity without a planning buffer.
Do not sync to ClickUp before validating epic and milestone structure.

faq.question: What planning model does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses quarters, epics, milestones, and two-week sprints as the main planning levels.

faq.question: How does it estimate team capacity?
faq.answer: It starts from 20 points per developer per sprint and recommends a 15 percent buffer.

faq.question: Can it create detailed product specs?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on roadmap planning and leaves detailed specifications to other tools.

faq.question: Does it replace issue tracking?
faq.answer: No. It keeps milestones coarse and expects GitHub, ClickUp, or another tracker for execution details.

faq.question: Can it support ClickUp workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents how epics and milestones map to ClickUp tasks and subtasks.

faq.question: Does it make planning decisions automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes collaborative commands that keep the user involved in key decisions.
